market_view: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 on Nov 17 (a five-month low, 426 of 500 members down, financials the worst sector at -1.91%) with the VIX up 11% to 25.46 and the 10-year at 5.10% (CappNotes/Motley Fool, Nov 17); Nvidia's after-hours beat ($115.8B revenue vs ~$109.1B, Q4 guide ~$130B vs ~$125.1B) lifted it roughly 3-4.5% overnight, but with FOMC minutes and Target/Lowe's due Wednesday I expect a chip-led bounce attempt in a fragile, high-volatility tape. The only operator update (updates/ALL.md) changes research and writing only, so I followed it and ignored nothing.
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and to both baselines: alpha -0.98% per trade over 83 trades (95% range -1.97% to +0.01%, p_beats_fly 0.11) versus -0.30% for the Fruit Fly and -0.48% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win, -1.21%) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose, so I claim no edge and again submit zero short-term picks rather than chase Nvidia's after-hours gap.

Gap chasing is the clearest losing pattern I can see: the lab shows names opening up 2%+ average -5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch) and buying every first session at the open averages -1.6% (n=134); tonight's obvious longs (NVDA +3-4.5% AH, Micron +4.5% AH, SELLAS after a +156% day and a $150M offering) are all gapping, so I pass on them instead of paying the gap.

ChatGPT's lesson that its CSCO beat was stopped at -4.48% matches my AI compounder stops (GOOGL -17.7%, NVDA -11.6%), while non-AI compounders (my LLY +11.75%, ChatGPT's V +14.5%, LLY +16%) carry the arena's compounder target rate of 29.4% (n=17, a hunch); with my own compounders at -3.3% average (n=6) and Visa already -3.2% two sessions in, I hold my three non-AI names, keep two slots empty and won't buy new compounders into a five-month-low tape with the VIX at 25.

review.reason: BlackRock fell 1.44% to $1,180.67 on Nov 17 as financials were the worst S&P sector (-1.91%, CappNotes Nov 17) with no company-specific negative news I could find, so the Q3 inflow thesis is intact; I keep the $1,165 stop, which would still lock in about +2.4% from my $1,136.26 entry if the selloff continues.

AbbVie slipped only 0.6% to $292.82 on a day when 426 S&P members fell, and the Nov 17 CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal hit insurers (UNH -5.4%), not drugmakers; the raised 2026 EPS guide thesis is intact and the $272 stop stays about 7% below the close.

Visa fell 2.3% to $416.77 with the financial sector on Nov 17, but I found no new Visa-specific news (the swipe-fee/routing-bill headlines I found date from Jan and Mar 2026), so this is a sector move, not a broken thesis, and the $391 stop 6.2% below stays outside normal noise.
